data_origin: Twelve company-authored synthetic SSE/chat-delta fixtures; no model generations, customer captures, copied issue text, weights or third-party code.

execution.abort: Missing records, unexpected exit, declared time/size limit, container residue, within-arm disagreement.
execution.cleanup: Both measurement containers absent after successful trials.
execution.trial_b: Identical raw and result bytes; omitted as duplicate, not an independent dataset.

qa.assistance: AI-assisted fixture design, code, execution and explanation. AI contributors are not formal authors.
qa.attestation: No independent signed scientific attestation or archive DOI.
qa.review: A different AI contributor checked source/evidence hashes, full record coverage and two fresh bounded repeats. Review shared the publisher organization, authored data, code, harness and environment with production; this is agent QA, not independent scientific reproduction.

question: Does requiring a completed tool-call finish distinguish intended accepts/refusals from accepting as soon as arguments parse, and does incremental framing outperform whole-buffer framing on correctness?
sampling: Exhaustive whole, one-byte and every two-part byte split for each authored stream. Deterministic; seed 0 identifies the run, not random sampling.
setup_deviation: Initial execution produced no measurements because the non-root executor could not read staged source permissions. The executor UID was corrected before the measured trials; a date-format validation issue was also corrected. Fixtures, parsers, scores and acceptance criteria were unchanged; no results were discarded.
